problem: A particle starts moving from the point with position vector $(i-4j)\,\text{km}$ with a constant velocity of $i\,\text{km/h}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $2$ hours.

feedback.problem: A particle moves from the origin with a constant velocity of  $(2i+5j)\,\text{cm/s}.$ Find the position vector of the particle after $3$ seconds.
feedback.worked_solution:
If a particle moves with constant velocity $u,$  the position vector of the particle at time $t$ can be found using

$$
r={r}_{0}+ut,
$$

 
where ${r}_{0}$ is the initial position of the particle.

In our case, we have

$$
{r}_{0}=0i+0j,\,u=2i+5j.
$$

Therefore, the position vector of the particle after $t=3\,\text{s}$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}r & ={r}_{0}+ut \\  & =(0i+0j)+(2i+5j)(3) \\  & =(6i+15j)\,\text{cm}.\end{aligned}
$$
